subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should OpenClaw's provider-usage runtime temporarily read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles for canonical OpenAI usage, or should affected users run `openclaw doctor --fix` before usage status works?
rationale: The PR has focused proof for a real upgrade gap, but it deliberately creates a runtime compatibility exception to the current canonical `openai` plus doctor-migration policy.

options.title: Confirm the usage-only bridge
options.body: Accept that `status --usage` may read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want affected users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before usage status reads legacy profile state.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require a follow-up patch that documents or further constrains the fallback to the proven provider-usage status path and removal boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm the usage-only bridge
recommendation.body: Accept that `status --usage` may read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored and merged the provider identity migration that defines the canonical `openai` boundary this PR would soften.
